items.text: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
The public /groups/:name/members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 for every group, but the public route and template have no pagination controls, so members after the 50th cannot be reached
{{#unless automatic}} inside an itemView likely resolves against the member, not the group, in Ember 1.x, so the remove link shows on automatic groups
group[usernames] parameter is now ignored in the API
'== 0' at lines 7 and 12 breaks .jshintrc eqeqeq rule

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
GET /groups/:name/members defaults to limit 50 for all groups, but the public group members page has no pagination controls, so members after the 50th are unreachable
remove_member using group.users.delete likely doesn't decrement groups.user_count counter_cache, while add_members uses group.add, making the two endpoints inconsistent
add_members does usernames.split(','), assuming a string; usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b yields an Array and NoMethodError -> 500

Item-view template references `member`, but that alias is not available inside a separate `itemView` template. The row will render with missing member data, and clicking remove can throw when the controller calls `member.get(...)`.
The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec sends xhr :put, :remove_member but the route is DELETE; it passes only because controller specs skip routing, so it tests the wrong HTTP verb
limit/offset params on the public members endpoint are unvalidated: negative values reach SQL (PostgreSQL rejects -> 500) and there is no upper cap on limit
Spec uses xhr :put for remove_member but the route is defined as DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members - using PUT can let the spec pass while the real route/verb would behave differently
The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
usernames input is not cleared after add operation, making it easy to accidentally re-add the same usernames

add_members calls group.add(user) with no existing-membership check; adding an existing member violates the unique index on group_users(group_id,user_id), raising RecordNotUnique -> 500, and earlier users in the list stay committed (no transaction)
totalPages calculation has off-by-one error when user_count is a multiple of limit - Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an extra page for exact multiples, should use Math.ceil instead
Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty page because findMembers keeps the old offset
The existing pending 'ensures that membership can be paginated' spec is still pending and parses the old array shape instead of the new {members, meta} response contract
group.save plus render_json_error after add/remove is a no-op: membership writes already hit the DB via has_many :through, so the error branch only fires on unrelated group validation failures

The automatic variable may not be in scope for the item view template - if it resolves against the member context it may be undefined, causing the remove control to show even for automatic groups, which would allow clicking remove and likely surface a 422 without UI handling

The group member row template hides the remove link using {{#unless automatic}}, but row context is a member (Discourse.User), so automatic is undefined and the remove link is shown even for automatic groups. Clicking it triggers a 422 (server blocks automatic group membership changes) and the UI ignores the rejected promise

`totalPages` is off by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, so the pager shows an extra page. Should use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` instead of `Math.floor(...) + 1`.
GET /groups/:name/members now returns {members, meta} instead of an array, breaking backwards compatibility

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 members with limit 50 shows 1/2 pages and Next loads an empty page); should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) which performs a direct SQL DELETE bypassing ActiveRecord callbacks including counter_cache, causing group.user_count to become stale after member removal. Should use group.remove(User.find(user_id)) instead which properly triggers counter cache updates.

offset = params[:offset].to_i can produce negative offsets and limit can be <= 0, which may raise or produce invalid queries in ActiveRecord - need to clamp/sanitize limit and offset before calling .limit(...).offset(...)
addMembers ends with '})' without a semicolon; jshint W033 'Missing semicolon' under .jshintrc, and CI runs 'jshint .' so CI should fail
Stray semicolon after block (if (!this.get('id')) { return };) -> jshint W032; spacing around return and DELETE object breaks CONTRIBUTING conventions
Route parameter mismatch - routes provide :id but controller expects :group_id, causing param is missing error

totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 which produces an off-by-one error when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100/50 gives 3 instead of 2), allowing users to navigate to an empty page. Should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Group#usernames= setter, destroy_deletions and after_save :destroy_deletions are now dead code in production (only specs call the setter)
create never reads params[:alias_level] although the form shows and sends it; value is silently dropped on create
Usernames are not normalized before lookup in add_members - whitespace or blank entries will silently skip valid users
Pagination params limit and offset are not clamped - negative or very large values can trigger heavy queries or odd behavior

remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the existing Group#remove helper, which skips per-row cleanup and leaves the removed user's primary_group_id not cleared, causing the group to still show as post flair

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
removeMember/addMembers have no rejection handler (422/500 gives admin no feedback); input not cleared after add; rapid next/previous can race findMembers responses
totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members -> '1/2', next loads an empty page)

Breaking admin/public API change without compatibility: create/update read top-level params instead of group[...], group[usernames] ignored, PATCH /admin/groups/:id changes[add|delete] removed (legacy PATCH now silently sets visible=false since params[:visible] is nil), and /groups/:name/members returns {members, meta} instead of an array with no documentation
Stray closing tag with no matching opening tag in group/members.hbs template
Hardcoded colors #333 and #aaa in SCSS instead of SCSS variables may break theme consistency

remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove: the removed user's primary_group_id is not cleared and the counter_cache groups.user_count is not decremented because has_many :through delete uses delete_all without GroupUser callbacks

No spec for the new {members, meta} response; pending 'ensures that membership can be paginated' spec still parses the old array shape; no spec for duplicate add, removal cleanup, or nonexistent usernames in add_members; create and non-automatic update coverage removed without replacement
Test for automatic-group remove_member uses PUT instead of DELETE, which won't validate verb correctness
Guard condition in group/members.hbs checks model but loop iterates over members - if model is truthy but members is undefined/empty, table header renders with no rows
findMembers builds the URL from the bound, possibly unsaved name; editing the name then paging/adding/removing requests /groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json -> 404

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which over-counts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50/50 -> 2 pages), allowing next to set offset to user_count, yielding an empty last page and incorrect currentPage/totalPages display

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec sends xhr :put to remove_member but the route is DELETE; also hardcodes group id 1 instead of fabricating an automatic group
PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes[add|delete] endpoint is removed without documentation

`findMembers()` is called without awaiting its result, introducing a race condition. The template may render before members are available. Either return the promise from `setupController` or move the async call back to `afterModel`/`beforeModel` where the router will wait for it.

The patch breaks the public and admin API with no compatibility path: create and update read top-level params instead of group[...], causing legacy create to get blank name/422 and legacy update to silently set visible=false

Admin group pagination computes totalPages with floor()+1 and Next can set offset==user_count, making an extra empty page reachable for exact multiples of limit (e.g. 100 users @ limit 50), causing the UI to show a bogus page count and render an empty members list on the last navigation step
The commit body is empty, violating CONTRIBUTING §5's requirement for detailed description of breaking changes
The remove_member controller spec uses PUT for the automatic-group rejection case, but the route and client use DELETE. This test can pass while the real DELETE integration is broken
Offset clamped redundantly in next/previous actions and again in findMembers
next() function allows navigating to an empty page by clamping offset to user_count instead of the last valid offset

issues.claim: The public GET /groups/:name/members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 for every group, but the public route and template have no pagination controls, so members after the 50th cannot be reached.

In the group member row itemView, {{#unless automatic}} resolves against the member (Discourse.User) rather than the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the remove link is shown for automatic groups.

The item-view template references `member`, but that alias is not available inside a separate itemView template, so rows render without member data and remove can fail when the controller calls member.get(...).
A function has code paths that end without an explicit return and return undefined.
The group[usernames] parameter is now ignored by the API.
The admin group create and update actions read top-level params instead of group[...], with no compatibility path: legacy create gets a blank name (422) and legacy update silently sets visible=false.
GET /groups/:name/members now returns {members, meta} instead of an array, which is not backwards compatible.
The PATCH /admin/groups/:id endpoint with changes[add|delete] is removed without documentation.
The '== 0' comparisons at lines 7 and 12 violate the .jshintrc eqeqeq rule.
totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which gives one extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 gives 3), so navigation can reach an empty page.
The next action clamps the offset to user_count instead of the last valid offset, so it can navigate to an empty page (e.g. total equal to limit gives offset == total).
remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which bypasses callbacks so the groups.user_count counter_cache is not decremented, unlike add_members which uses group.add.
remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove, so the removed user's primary_group_id is not cleared and the group can still show as post flair.
add_members calls usernames.split(','), assuming a string; usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b yields an Array and raises NoMethodError (500).
The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' controller spec sends xhr :put to remove_member, but the route is DELETE; it passes only because controller specs skip routing.
The limit and offset params on the members endpoint are not validated or clamped: negative values reach SQL and cause errors, and limit has no upper cap.
findMembers() is called asynchronously without its promise being returned or awaited from setupController, so the template may render before member data is available.
removeMember and addMembers have no rejection handler, so 422/500 responses give the admin no feedback.
The usernames input is not cleared after an add operation.

add_members calls group.add(user) without checking for existing membership, so adding an existing member violates the unique index on group_users(group_id,user_id) and raises RecordNotUnique (500), and earlier users stay committed because there is no transaction.
Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty page because findMembers keeps the old offset.
The pending 'ensures that membership can be paginated' spec still parses the old array shape, and no spec covers the new {members, meta} response contract.

group.save with render_json_error after add/remove is effectively a no-op, because membership writes already hit the DB via has_many :through, so the error branch only fires on unrelated group validation failures.
addMembers ends with '})' without a semicolon, which triggers jshint W033 under .jshintrc.
There is a stray semicolon after a block (if (!this.get('id')) { return };), which triggers jshint W032.
The routes provide the group id in params[:id], but the controller reads params[:group_id], causing a param-missing failure.
The Group#usernames= setter, destroy_deletions and after_save :destroy_deletions are now dead code in production; only specs call the setter.
The create action never reads params[:alias_level], although the form sends it, so the value is dropped on create.
add_members does not normalize usernames before lookup, so whitespace or blank entries cause valid users to be skipped.
The group/members.hbs template contains a stray closing tag with no matching opening tag.
The SCSS hardcodes the colors #333 and #aaa instead of using SCSS variables.
The guard in group/members.hbs checks model, but the loop iterates over members, so the table header can render with no rows.
findMembers builds its URL from the bound, possibly unsaved group name, so after the name is edited, paging/add/remove request /groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json and get a 404.
The commit body is empty, contrary to CONTRIBUTING §5's requirement to describe breaking changes.
The offset is clamped in the next/previous actions and again in findMembers.
